description: Json.unicode/4 encodes every \\uXXXX value independently as a three-byte sequence. fz therefore accepts lone high and low surrogates as invalid UTF-8 and renders a valid pair such as \\uD83D\\uDE00 as two invalid three-byte sequences. Elixir reports unexpected_end for an unpaired high surrogate, unexpected_sequence for an unpaired low surrogate, and joins the pair into the four-byte UTF-8 encoding. Add Elixir-oracled value/key fixtures across interp, run, and build; make one Unicode escape authority join and validate surrogate pairs; update decoder documentation.

comments.text: Implemented in e460a0741. Json now treats UTF-16 surrogate syntax as one decision: valid high/low pairs join into one Unicode scalar, lone lows and complete non-low followers report Elixir-compatible unexpected_sequence spans, and incomplete highs report unexpected_end. The joined scalar and ordinary escapes go through new Utf8.from_codepoint/1, which checks the Unicode scalar domain and delegates byte encoding to the existing ::utf8 bitstring authority; Json private UTF-8 encoding was removed. Added an Elixir-oracled 16-case value/key fixture, direct scalar-width/range boundary coverage, Json and Utf8 public docs, and semantic-authority docs. Proven red in interp/run/build before implementation. Final green: JSON 36/36, UTF-8 24/24, full fixture matrix 709/709, compiler library 2018 passed/6 known ignored, runtime 260/260, CLI 30/30, doctests, AOT integration, clippy -D warnings, fmt, diff check, and pre-commit gates.
Draft PR: https://github.com/jallum/fz/pull/135 (stacked on #134). Remote lint and test checks are green.

title: Json.decode emits invalid UTF-8 for Unicode surrogate escapes
